court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Thane, in Petition No.A-192 of 2017
case_name: Mala Kundan Rai @ Mala Rajeev Agarwal vs Rajeev Ramgopal Agarwal

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Appellant-wife, Mala Kundan Rai @ Mala Rajeev Agarwal

facts_of_case: The parties were married on 30 November, 2013. The husband filed a petition for annulment of the marriage, which was declared null and void by the trial court. The wife appeals against this decision.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party who alleges suppression to prove that there was actual suppression.
legal_principles.held: We find from the scrutiny of Petitioner's cross examination, that it is the Respondent's case that entire past history of the Respondent was informed to Petitioner by Respondent's friend 'Soumya' prior to the marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A party's admission in cross-examination can be used as evidence to prove their case.
legal_principles.held: The Learned Counsel for Petitioner submits that the admissions given by the Respondent in her cross examination proves that Respondent had suppressed the fact that she was married to Ashok Yadav and that she had a son from the said wedlock.

outcome.final_order: The final order is not specified in this excerpt.
